Computer Technology and engineering applications combine electrical function with physical interfaces. Fabrication is valuable when it makes a circuit safer to test, a cable route legible, an enclosure serviceable, or a user interaction easier to evaluate.

## Project directions

:::: {.ter-project-grid}
::: {.ter-project-card}
### PCB layout and soldering fixture
<p class="ter-course-code">TEJ2O · Gauge / fixture family</p>
Design a low-force fixture that locates a small board and selected components while students plan or inspect assembly.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Measure PCB → locate keep-outs → prototype supports → fit test</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>2.54 mm pitch, datums, board clearance, CAD, tolerance</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate · under 180 × 120 mm</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Laser-cut sheet or heat-resistant printed parts selected for the task</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Support the board without flexing or loading components</dd><dt>Use boundary</dt><dd>Keep combustible fixtures away from hot soldering work unless material is approved</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=computer-technology&type=jigs-gauges">PCB and cable gauges</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../04-3d-printing/03-tolerances-functional-parts.qmd">Tolerances & Functional Parts</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Add interchangeable board locators with a documented interface</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Test-lead and cable module
<p class="ter-course-code">TEJ2O / senior TEJ · Portable work module</p>
Organize leads and cables by function so they deploy without tangling and return to a visible inventory.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Workflow study → bend-radius check → comb prototypes → carry/use test</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Cable geometry, strain relief, labelling, modular interfaces</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Introductory–intermediate · under 300 mm wide</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Plywood face, printed clips, or flexible retainers</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Avoid sharp edges and loads on connectors</dd><dt>Use boundary</dt><dd>Disconnect and de-energize leads before storage</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=computer-technology&type=tool-holders">Electronics organizers</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../03-laser-cutting/07-wall-bench-module.qmd">Wall + Bench Module</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Add visual status for tested, suspect, and repair-needed leads</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Serviceable sensor enclosure
<p class="ter-course-code">Senior TEJ · Organizer / enclosure family</p>
Enclose a low-voltage sensor project while preserving airflow, connector access, mounting, and repair.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Requirements → component keep-outs → CAD → fit coupon → enclosure → thermal observation</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Interfaces, tolerances, ventilation, fastening, assembly drawing</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate–advanced · device-sized</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Printed polymer or sheet assembly suitable for classroom voltage and temperature</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Mount boards at defined points; protect cables from pullout</dd><dt>Use boundary</dt><dd>No mains voltage; account for heat and battery requirements</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=computer-technology&type=core-geometry">Fan and mounting patterns</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../04-3d-printing/04-design-challenge.qmd">3D Printing Design Challenge</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Perform a timed service task and redesign the enclosure access</dd></dl>
:::
::::
